utilitarian.author: Jeremy Bentham
utilitarian.source: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation (1789)
utilitarian.text: The greatest happiness of the greatest number is the foundation of morals and legislation.

deontological.author: Immanuel Kant
deontological.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
deontological.text: Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.

care.author: Joan Tronto
care.source: Moral Boundaries: A Political Argument for an Ethic of Care
care.text: Attentiveness, responsibility, competence, and responsiveness are the four phases of care that together constitute the practice of care ethics.

virtue.author: Aristotle
virtue.text: Virtue, then, being of two kinds, intellectual and moral, intellectual virtue in the main owes both its birth and its growth to teaching, while moral virtue comes about as a result of habit... it is by doing just acts that the just man is produced, and by doing temperate acts the temperate man...

rawlsian.author: John Rawls
rawlsian.text: Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought. The principles of justice are chosen behind a veil of ignorance to ensure impartiality.
